Secure Your Financial Future with Adams County’s Tax Lien Sale

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course

Adams County, Illinois, is not just a place with a rich history; it’s also a prime spot for tax lien investing. The annual tax lien sale, held every October, offers potential returns of up to 54% over three years. With a population of around 66,000, Adams County might seem small, but it offers big investment opportunities.

Understanding Tax Lien Certificates

Tax lien certificates represent unpaid property taxes. When you buy a tax lien certificate, you’re essentially paying someone’s taxes in exchange for a high interest rate. If the property owner doesn’t pay the taxes within a redemption period (2.5 to 3 years), you can start the process of owning the property.

Steps to Start Tax Lien Investing in Adams County

Research and Understand Local Laws

Knowing the legal framework is crucial. Adams County’s regulations ensure that investors understand the bidding process and redemption periods.

Visit the Local Treasurer’s Website

The Treasurer’s site provides comprehensive details about tax sales: County Treasurer’s Office.

Check the Auction Site

Auctions are held at the Adams County Courthouse, Courtroom 2D. For more information, visit the Adams County Tax Sale page.

Read the Details about Tax Liens

Understand sale schedules, parcel inquiries, and other essential details provided on the county’s official website.

Contact the County Office

For additional inquiries, you can reach out directly to the Adams County Treasurer’s Office.

Important Details

Pro Tips

  • Register Early: Ensure your registration and IRS Form W-9 are submitted by October for the upcoming sale.
  • Understand Bidding: Bids start at 9%, and the certificate goes to the lowest bidder, maximizing your potential returns.
  • Post-Sale Opportunities: Pay subsequent taxes starting around September each year to keep your investment active.

FAQs

Q: What happens if the property owner doesn’t redeem the tax lien?

A: You can initiate the process to own the property, paying only the back taxes and associated fees.

Q: How do I participate in the tax lien sale?

A: Register at least ten business days before the sale, complete the required forms, and attend the auction at the Adams County Courthouse.

For more information and useful links, visit the County’s official website or the dedicated tax sale pages listed above.

If you have questions or need guidance, don’t hesitate to contact the County Treasurer’s Office or visit their website.
